explanation: The key idea is convergence: different methods can reach a valid representation of the same domain facts. The methods are not identical in procedure, but a correct result from either should be faithful to the business reality being modeled.

options.text: Different design methods can still converge on a schema that captures the same underlying facts.
Only the conceptual method can produce a schema that avoids anomalies.
Normalization and conceptual modeling always produce identical SQL statements.
A correct schema must preserve every intermediate design decision made during analysis.

prompt: Two analysts independently design a database for the same company. One uses normalization rules; the other uses a conceptual modeling method. They disagree on the process but both claim the final schema is correct. What is the strongest reason this can happen?

source.title: Normalization and other Data Modeling Methods
